l: Mitigating the Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) via Pure Synthetic Data, Mitigating the Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) via Pure Synthetic Data, Abstract
s: The text concerns retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems that use external knowledge sources, including private data. It introduces SAGE, a two-stage paradigm for generating synthetic data as a privacy-preserving alternative to retrieval data. SAGE first preserves key contextual information through attribute-based extraction and generation, then improves privacy through agent-based iterative refinement. Experiments show that synthetic retrieval data achieves comparable performance to original data while substantially reducing privacy risks.

s: The unit explains that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) combines retrieved information with a user query for a large language model, but retrieval from private data can cause serious information leakage. It proposes using synthetic data instead of original data as retrieval context to reduce privacy risks while preserving useful information. The authors introduce SAGE, a two-stage method that first generates synthetic retrieval data from extracted attributes and key information, then iteratively refines it through privacy assessment and rewriting agents. Experiments show that synthetic retrieval data can achieve comparable performance to original data while substantially reducing privacy risks.

l: Mitigating the Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) via Pure Synthetic Data, Mitigating the Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) via Pure Synthetic Data, Related Works
s: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), introduced by Lewis et al. (2020), improves the accuracy and relevance of large language model outputs and can reduce hallucinations, but it is vulnerable to privacy attacks and information extraction. Huang et al. (2023), Zeng et al. (2024), and Qi et al. (2024) document privacy leakage and attacks affecting retrieval-based language models and production RAG systems. Researchers including Ye et al. (2022), Meng et al. (2022), and Gao et al. (2023a) use large language models to generate synthetic data for downstream tasks and improve its quality and diversity. Tang et al. (2023) and Xie et al. propose privacy-preserving synthetic data methods, but the described data is not guaranteed to retain contextual information from the original data and therefore may not fit RAG systems well.

l: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), Mitigating the Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) via Pure Synthetic Data, Related Works
s: Retrieval-augmented generation was introduced by Lewis et al. (2020) and improves output accuracy and relevance while mitigating hallucinations. Its architecture allows updates to the dataset, retriever, and large language model without retraining, supporting applications such as personal chatbots and specialized domain experts. It is vulnerable to extraction attacks and other privacy attacks, including attacks against production RAG models.

s: Privacy issues arise in retrieval-based language models and RAG systems. Huang et al. (2023) identified privacy leakage in KNN-LM, while Zeng et al. (2024) and Qi et al. (2024) showed that RAG systems, including production models, are vulnerable to extraction and other attacks.

s: The ablation studies investigate how model choice, the number of attributes, and the number of retrieved documents per query affect synthetic data quality and privacy.
